newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria completes sowing of 1.5 mln hectares.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria completes sowing of 1.5 mln hectares.

text.p: Bulgaria has completed autumn sowing of 1.5 million hectares of wheat and barley, nearly meeting its target of 1.6 million ha of grain, an agriculture ministry official said on Wednesday.

"We consider this year's sowing successful as wheat sowings have covered some 1.2 million hectares, while some 280,000 hectares have been sown with barley," ministry spokeswoman Roza Trichkova told Reuters.
In 1995 Bulgaria planted one million ha to wheat and 270,000 to barley.
Trichkova said Bulgaria would not face bread shortages next year as enough wheat for human consumption had been sown.
She added, "1996 will be the last year with a grain problem for the country."
Debt-ridden Bulgaria initially delayed its autumn sowing of wheat and barley due to a lack of funds and incentives to farmers and because of record high interest rates for loans.
To speed up sowing and stave off further shortages, parliament passed a law in October unblocking farmers' funds from banks placed in receivership by the central bank.
Under the bill, the domestic purchase prices for wheat, maize and barley from the 1996/97 harvest will be no less than 80 percent of the international price.
Trichkova said those measures, plus favourable weather conditions which prolonged the planting period, boosted autumn sowings.
Last year low domestic prices encouraged high exports, which combined with a poor harvest last summer to produce an acute grain shortage.
